claims.claim_text: Without tape feeders a pick-and-place machine is not functionally a pick-and-place machine; it is a gantry.
claims.quote_verbatim: Without feeders, a pick and place machine is essentially useless.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Feeders are the defining subsystem: components must be dispensed continuously rather than reloaded every hundred parts.
claims.quote_verbatim: It is not a pick and place until you've got tape feeders. You have to have tape feeders.
claims.speaker: Mike Harrison

claims.claim_text: An XY head without feeders is a toy, since jelly-bean parts must be dispensed indefinitely without operator intervention.
claims.quote_verbatim: But without feeders, it's a toy
claims.speaker: Mike Harrison

claims.claim_text: Anyone designing a machine should design the feeder first, the motion system being comparatively straightforward: XY motors, camera, software and a vacuum head.
claims.quote_verbatim: design a feeder first
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Feeders dominate machine cost, at roughly 500 dollars each, and are the subsystem an owner most wants more of.
claims.quote_verbatim: the feeders are often the, the, the expensive part
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Feeders carry part identity and configuration, completing the machine in the way a cartridge completes a console.
claims.quote_verbatim: the Nintendo is not complete until you put a cartridge in it
claims.speaker: Chris Denney

claims.claim_text: Feeder slot count is a hard constraint on the bill of materials: exceeding the machine's loader count forces a second setup pass and a second setup cost.
claims.quote_verbatim: if you have a machine that can do 40 different loaders
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Last Minute Decisions - Obdurate Onepercenter Obstacles

claims.claim_text: The same threshold effect applies at 60 feeders and 61 distinct parts, which is the practical argument for BOM consolidation.
claims.quote_verbatim: if machines haven't got 60 feeders
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Integrated parts are bought partly for BOM convenience, occupying one feeder slot where discrete equivalents would occupy four.
claims.quote_verbatim: it's a single reel on your pick and place machine instead of four reels
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Every machine handles 0603; 0402 is a capability step that not all machines clear, requiring different nozzles and costing yield, so smaller packages should not be specified without need.
claims.quote_verbatim: Every pick-and-place machine will do 0603 as a minimum
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Ceramic capacitors & High end scopes - Kempt Kickstarter Kakorrhaphiophobia

claims.claim_text: Package size filters the supplier list rather than merely raising cost: 0402 is placeable by roughly 65 percent of machines and 0201 by roughly 30 percent.
claims.quote_verbatim: It's now down to 65% of all the machines and 0201, 30% of the machines
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Panel dimensions must be agreed with the assembler, not only the fabricator: PCB houses quote large panels that will not fit a pick-and-place machine, a mismatch companies discover after the boards are made.
claims.quote_verbatim: that often won't fit in a pick and place machine
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: A large V-scored panel supported only at its guide rails will fail mechanically under placement head pressure.
claims.quote_verbatim: Your board will just snap in half as soon as the head hits it
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Tooling strips carrying sprocket holes along the panel edge are what allow a board to be transported through the machine.
claims.quote_verbatim: with the socket holes in them that allow your pick and place machine to take your board through
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: An assembly line is physically a line: stencil printer, pick-and-place, reflow oven, optical inspection and bed-of-nails test, connected by conveyor.
claims.quote_verbatim: It literally is a row of pick and place machines with the conveyor belt
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: The same sequence was described as separate machines joined by a conveyor, from paste dispensing through placement and reflow to automated visual inspection.
claims.quote_verbatim: then it goes into the reflow oven, and then to the automated visual inspection
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Solder paste is applied before placement because its tack retains parts until reflow.
claims.quote_verbatim: the paste is sticky and tacky. So those parts don't go anywhere
claims.speaker: Chris Denney

claims.claim_text: A machine cannot detect that the wrong reel was loaded into a slot; the error surfaces only at automated optical inspection after assembly.
claims.quote_verbatim: the pick and place machine assumes that you've put the correct part in the correct slot
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Assemblers require excess components beyond the board count, because parts are consumed during reel loading and setup.
claims.quote_verbatim: you can't give your manufacturer a reel of 100 resistors and expect them to populate 100 boards
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Solar Cells, SparkFun, TSMC - The Detroit Debunking

claims.claim_text: Cut-tape reels with leader tape do not solve the excess-component problem, since the machine consumes a large fraction of a short reel.
claims.quote_verbatim: But then the machine ends up just wasting half of them anyway
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Most machines are natively metric and convert from imperial input, which introduces cascading rounding errors in placement data.
claims.quote_verbatim: speak metric natively
claims.speaker: Jonathan Hirschman
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Jonathan Hirschman of PCB:NG

claims.claim_text: Operating a machine changes design practice, because nozzle changes and part handling become visible constraints at schematic and layout time.
claims.quote_verbatim: having a pick and places definitely made me a better design engineer
claims.speaker: Ryan O'Hara
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Ryan O'Hara - Keyed, Kerfed Kapton

claims.claim_text: A mature in-house process aligns CAD library part orientation with feeder tape orientation, so that placement rotation needs no per-job checking.
claims.quote_verbatim: all my PCB library parts are the same way around as the tape in my feeders
claims.speaker: Mike Harrison

claims.claim_text: Pickup is tuned per component: nozzle dwell time, vacuum level and release timing are all adjustable and all need setting.
claims.quote_verbatim: do you have enough suction? Do you release at the right time?
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Desktop machines target low to medium volume and in-house prototype batches rather than production.
claims.quote_verbatim: It's meant for people that are doing a batch of prototypes in house
claims.speaker: Stephen Hawes
claims.episode_title: A Benchtop Pick and Place with Stephen Hawes

claims.claim_text: Standardising on a common parts library and permanently loading many machines fails on combinatorics; workable high-mix assembly treats placement as one step among many, with material handling as the dominant problem.
claims.quote_verbatim: Material handling is a huge thing
claims.speaker: Andrew Seddon
claims.episode_title: CircuitHub, 12 Years Later with Andrew Seddon

claims.claim_text: Holds that the window in which a self-operated machine beats outsourced assembly on combined time and money is very narrow.
claims.quote_verbatim: there's a very narrow window of where a do-it-yourself pick and place machine makes sense
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Shop bots, 450 mm fabs & redFrog - Pick and Place Palillogy

claims.claim_text: Estimates that roughly nine in ten people who believe they need a machine do not.
claims.quote_verbatim: there's probably a 90% chance that you don't
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Sets the volume threshold at around a hundred boards; below that, manual assembly is faster overall.
claims.quote_verbatim: if you're doing 10 boards you know often it's not worth your time
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Guns and Mobile Labs - Nuanced Nomadic Non-essentials

claims.claim_text: Argues on opportunity cost that the purchase price of a low-cost machine buys a large quantity of professional assembly.
claims.quote_verbatim: buys me an awful lot of assembly time on a professional pick-and-place machine
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Agrees with the 90 percent estimate but holds that falling entry cost is shifting it, and that high-mix low-volume work with fast turnaround is now a genuine case for ownership.
claims.quote_verbatim: I think that's changing with the decreasing cost, the entry cost
claims.speaker: Mike Harrison

claims.claim_text: Characterises the difficulty as many small problems rather than one large one, which is why it is underestimated before ownership.
claims.quote_verbatim: It's lots and lots and lots and lots of tiny, tiny issues. And little ones that will kill you.
claims.speaker: Mike Harrison

claims.claim_text: Argues that falling cost and rising accessibility have made ownership defensible where sufficient recurring demand exists.
claims.quote_verbatim: maybe it is worth the time to do your own things
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Frames the real cost as a change of profession: an owner becomes a process engineer concerned with paste thickness and placement statistics rather than an electrical engineer.
claims.quote_verbatim: You become a process engineer. You don't become an electrical engineer.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Impedance Matching" with Davidson and Vandenbout - Presbytes Pushing Portfolios

claims.claim_text: Proposes a usage test: a machine used less than weekly represents money better spent elsewhere.
claims.quote_verbatim: unless you're using it at least weekly, there may be better things you could be spending your money on
claims.speaker: Dafydd Roche

claims.claim_text: Identifies learning rather than profit as the honest motive for most owners.
claims.quote_verbatim: You buy it because you want to learn something
claims.speaker: Dafydd Roche

claims.claim_text: Declines ownership at batch sizes around fifty on the grounds of learning time rather than purchase price.
claims.quote_verbatim: It's not just the cost of the pick in place. It's the learning
claims.speaker: Ian Johnston

claims.claim_text: Rejects the premise outright.
claims.quote_verbatim: I don't really need a pick and place machine. I am a pick and place machine.
claims.speaker: Jeff Keyzer

claims.claim_text: Argues that headline prices for crowdfunded machines exclude the options needed to make them usable, at which point commercial machines are already available.
claims.quote_verbatim: it can be anywhere from $300 to $3,000 depending on the options
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Warming Up To IoT - Tendentious Thermal Tools

claims.claim_text: Rejects a crowdfunded machine's one-touch setup claim while crediting its custom feeder design.
claims.quote_verbatim: I'm calling BS on that. There's no way you can do a one touch setup.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Frames the test for a low-cost machine as whether the entry price buys something expandable into a working machine or a fixed toy.
claims.quote_verbatim: If $300 is your entry cost for a machine that can be made usable, great.
claims.speaker: Mike Harrison

claims.claim_text: Argues the industry optimises the wrong specifications, and that a genuinely working sub-5000-dollar machine would lack the structure to carry full reels.
claims.quote_verbatim: those specs are geared towards the wrong problem
claims.speaker: Jonathan Hirschman
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Jonathan Hirschman of PCB:NG

claims.claim_text: Attributes poor industrial machine software to switching costs: a buyer locked into a 50,000-dollar machine will tolerate any interface.
claims.quote_verbatim: It doesn't matter how bad the software is
claims.speaker: Stephen Hawes
claims.episode_title: A Benchtop Pick and Place with Stephen Hawes

claims.claim_text: A 40,000-dollar secondhand Juki bought around 2000 for an in-house line repaid its cost within four months, given continuous internal demand, a dedicated operator and prior subcontractor spending.
claims.quote_verbatim: after the first four months, the machine was paid for
claims.speaker: Vincent Himpe
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Vincent Himpe - Escaped Electron Elocution

claims.claim_text: Describes an in-house placement decision as a mistake made against a co-founder's objection.
claims.quote_verbatim: we did it the wrong way
claims.speaker: Joe Garrison
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Joe and Mark Garrison - Subtly Spelling SayLeeAy

claims.claim_text: Traces the root cause to a design decision to minimise board size, which forced 0201 placement.
claims.quote_verbatim: we decided to make the board, you know, as small and as cool as possible
claims.speaker: Joe Garrison
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Joe and Mark Garrison - Subtly Spelling SayLeeAy

claims.claim_text: The selected machine was specified for the required package size but had no customer running it that way in production.
claims.quote_verbatim: no one had really pushed this machine as hard as we were going to push it
claims.speaker: Joe Garrison
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Joe and Mark Garrison - Subtly Spelling SayLeeAy

claims.claim_text: Recommends having the actual board built on the actual machine before purchase, and selecting machines that contract manufacturers run daily.
claims.quote_verbatim: have that board built by the machine, by that exact machine before you buy it
claims.speaker: Joe Garrison
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Joe and Mark Garrison - Subtly Spelling SayLeeAy

claims.claim_text: Notes that placement capability alone is insufficient, since a machine may achieve fine-pitch placement only at a large throughput penalty.
claims.quote_verbatim: if you have to take, you know, 80% more time per board
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Joe and Mark Garrison - Subtly Spelling SayLeeAy

claims.claim_text: Reports that machines require sustained attention to commission and to keep running, and that placement alone is insufficient without reflow and stencil equipment.
claims.quote_verbatim: These machines take a lot of babysitting
claims.speaker: Vic Aprea
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Vic Aprea - Federated Firmware Functionalism

claims.claim_text: A repeated-part panel ran without difficulty while the mixed-component side required per-part calibration and differing pick heights.
claims.quote_verbatim: It was not calibrated for the different types of components
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Achieved roughly 95 percent placement accuracy without extensive setup across 1,200 LEDs, the characteristic failure being parts standing on edge that vision accepted because the lens distorted the outline.
claims.quote_verbatim: without much setup, probably 95% accuracy
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Concluded from the exercise that panelising boards should be the default regardless of assembly method.
claims.quote_verbatim: I will always panelize boards from now on
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Acquired a machine on indefinite loan after the hackspace that owned it was evicted and its equipment needed storage.
claims.quote_verbatim: storage costs money, you know, why not store it at my house?
claims.speaker: Tim from Mitxela
claims.episode_title: LEDs Everywhere with Tim from Mitxela

claims.claim_text: During the 2021-22 component shortage at least one owner mothballed a working machine for lack of parts and space, raising the unresolved question of whether an idle machine must be exercised periodically.
claims.quote_verbatim: he's packing up his pick and place machine and putting it into mothballs
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Predicted in 2010 that falling machine prices would put in-house placement, reflow and paste dispensing within hobbyist reach within a decade, marking the shift from half-million-dollar to ten-thousand-dollar machines.
claims.quote_verbatim: they don't cost half a million dollars anymore. They cost 10 grand
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Open Hardware and The Creative Economy

claims.claim_text: An open-source machine was described as the outstanding unsolved problem in open hardware, defeated by mechanical complexity, with feeding mechanisms named as the reason machines cost what they do.
claims.quote_verbatim: Everyone's talking about it, but nobody does it because they realize, oh, shit, it's just too hard.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Analog Devices, Design Spark - Unusual Usenet Usurpation

claims.claim_text: By late 2013 Chinese desktop machines were available at around 5,000 dollars and reported to work acceptably.
claims.quote_verbatim: Chinese pick-and-place machine
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Secondhand professional machines from the mid-1990s were available in good condition at around 10,000 dollars.
claims.quote_verbatim: you can get one of these odds for like right around 10 K and really good shape
claims.speaker: Ryan O'Hara
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Ryan O'Hara - Keyed, Kerfed Kapton

claims.claim_text: By late 2022 a desktop machine with 40 integrated feeders was available under 3,000 dollars.
claims.quote_verbatim: Basically under 3K with like 40 feeders
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Picking a Pick and Place Pickiness

claims.claim_text: 3D Robotics bought a line because batching a thousand boards froze the design until the stock sold, whereas in-house placement permitted roughly thirty board revisions in a year.
claims.quote_verbatim: you can't change the design until you've sold all 1,000 of them
claims.speaker: Chris Anderson
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Chris Anderson - Deambulatory Daedal Drones

claims.claim_text: Professional machines place dozens of devices per second, completing a board in an hour or two.
claims.quote_verbatim: to see that thing go and place dozens of devices per second
claims.speaker: Eric Van Wyk
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Eric VanWyk - Meiotic Mountenance Mooshimeter
